$comment: Test vectors for the inbox hash.
The hash is computed independently by the auth-callout (to mint the subscribe permission)
and by this client (to pick its inbox), with no channel between them. When they disagree the
symptom is a request that times out with no error anywhere the caller can see, and the
violation is logged by the NATS server rather than returned to the client.
THESE VALUES ARE SYNTHETIC, and that limits what this file can prove: it pins the ALGORITHM
against regressions, not the agreement with the callout. Values captured from a real callout
would prove more, but they are the Zitadel subject ids of real accounts and do not belong in
The agreement itself is proved where real identities legitimately exist and are never
committed: test/integration/live.test.ts, against a real deployment. A wrong hash there means
the reply is published to an inbox nobody is subscribed to, so the request simply times out —
which is exactly what that suite asserts does not happen.
algorithm: lowercase(base32(sha256(userId))[0..16]), RFC 4648 alphabet, no padding.

vectors.note: the shape of a Zitadel subject id
a second one, so a change to the algorithm cannot pass by luck
